results.reader_title: Quantum technologies have very different levels of readiness
results.reader_what: JRC assesses 195 quantum signals; 12.9% are operational and many remain experimental.
results.reader_why: Different maturity levels call for staged investment, shared test facilities, standards and skills.

deep_analysis.qualification: The 195 identified quantum foresight signals measure technology readiness, not market penetration, policy effects or a causal EU advantage.

claims.qualification: The 195 identified quantum foresight signals measure technology readiness, not market penetration, policy effects or a causal EU advantage.

results.reader_what: EU tender research links security assessments with innovation outcomes only among tenders awarded to domestic suppliers.
results.reader_why: National security procedures can affect innovation procurement and may fragment the EU internal market.
results.reader_more: The researchers combine a pan-European survey of 1,613 procurements with EU Tenders Electronic Daily information. They report positive associations between national security assessments and innovation or critical-technology purchasing in domestic-award cases, not uniformly across all tenders. They warn that uncoordinated national assessment practices may impede cross-border competition.

deep_analysis.research_question: How do national security assessments affect EU procurement, innovation and critical technologies?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Security assessments correlate with innovation and critical-technology procurement when domestic bidders win, producing a cross-border trade-off.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Observational analysis of 1,613 EU procurement projects linked to TED public tender data.
deep_analysis.qualification: The observational study reports conditional associations, not causal proof; innovation and critical-technology benefits were seen only when domestic suppliers won the tender.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: A Route 2 directly measures European innovative procurement outcomes; Route 3 studies security-screening policy effects on EU research and innovation system.

claims.qualification: The observational study reports conditional associations, not causal proof; innovation and critical-technology benefits were seen only when domestic suppliers won the tender.
claims.text: A study of 1,613 EU procurement projects finds positive security-assessment associations with innovation and critical-technology outcomes only for domestic-award tenders.
